evidence_items.locator: Section Most organizations rehire laid-off employees within 6 months
evidence_items.explanation: The original survey reports completed refilling of roles following AI-led layoffs, alongside reports of unmet automation expectations and unexpectedly high human oversight needs. It supports the existence of reversals, although the published aggregates do not individually link every rehire to its cause.

evidence_items.publisher: The Wall Street Journal, syndicated by Mint
evidence_items.locator: Paragraph describing Lattice CEO Sarah Franklin's account of entry-level hiring
evidence_items.explanation: Franklin attributes renewed recruitment among clients partly to discovering that AI agents could not replace the expected human work. This supplies a contemporaneous causal account; the article also identifies growth and other reasons for hiring elsewhere.
The bank reversed proposed AI-related redundancies and allowed workers to remain. This supports continued human staffing needs, but it is not proof that dismissed workers were rehired.

This account reproduces Klarna's denial that its chief executive's quality remark concerned AI service failures. It limits reliance on Klarna as an example; the underlying SEC letter could not be read through read_page.
